narrativeReportMd:
# CoverageEligibilityRequest R4->R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No local R4-valid CoverageEligibilityRequest instance pattern was found that becomes invalid solely because of local CoverageEligibilityRequest element cardinality, type, reference-target, modifier, or required terminology changes. The main risks are migration/runtime risks from R6-only optional content and a semantic clarification of `provider`.

## Scope
This report covers the base CoverageEligibilityRequest resource definition only. Inherited Element/DomainResource changes and separate search/operation artifacts are out of scope.

## Main migration themes
R6 adds optional `statusReason` and `event` content. These are safe for R4-to-R6 validation because they are optional, but R6 instances using them cannot be represented losslessly in a plain R4 CoverageEligibilityRequest without extensions or a conversion policy. Existing common fields retain cardinalities, type choices, reference targets, modifier flags, and required code sets.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest practical impact is R6-to-R4 data loss for `event` and `statusReason`, plus business-rule ambiguity from the changed `provider` comment that now describes a billing-provider/data-accountability role.

## Findings requiring human review
`event` conversion needs a policy decision because it may overlap only partially with R4 `serviced[x]`. `provider` needs review because the R6 comment appears to narrow or redirect business meaning without a computable validation change.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The optional additions are generally compatible for forward validation, but they could have been represented for cross-version exchange through published extensions or conversion maps. The provider semantic change could have been less disruptive if the old requestor-oriented interpretation had been explicitly preserved or separated from billing-provider semantics.

## Follow-up analysis
Review base Element/DomainResource reports for inherited constraints and obtain any official R4/R6 conversion maps or ballot change notes for CoverageEligibilityRequest.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No hard local R4-to-R6 instance-breaking change was found. The main migration concerns are R6-only `statusReason`, R6-only `event`, and the changed business semantics in the `provider` comment. The largest uncertainty is the absence of official narrative change notes or cross-version maps for these changes.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migrations from R4 to R6 can generally preserve existing local CoverageEligibilityRequest content without mandatory new fields or narrowed datatypes. Reverse conversion from R6 to R4 is not lossless if R6 instances use `statusReason` or `event`; implementations should define extensions or profile-specific transforms. Business logic that treats `provider` as the requestor should be checked against R6's billing-provider/data-accountability wording.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural conclusions because both package StructureDefinitions were present and the local snapshots/differentials were compared. Confidence is medium for semantic intent because the package does not include an official resource-specific change explanation or conversion map, and the R6 provider comment uses claim-oriented wording that may need human interpretation.

findings.title: R6 adds optional summary element CoverageEligibilityRequest.statusReason

oldState.summary: No local status reason element existed in R4 CoverageEligibilityRequest.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could carry a cancellation or status-change explanation only through extensions or narrative; there was no base `statusReason` property.

newState.summary: R6 adds `statusReason` as an optional 0..1 string included in summaries.

semanticText.definition: Used to indicate why the status has changed.
semanticText.comment: Implementation guides may consider adding invariants such that if status = cancelled, statusReason SHALL be supplied.
semanticText.requirements: This is used to implement conformance on other elements.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 instances may carry a string explanation for why `status` changed; the base element remains optional and is not a modifier.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 element is a new local child of the resource with no R4 element id or semantically equivalent local base property.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a hard R4-to-R6 validation break because the new element is optional. It is a reverse-conversion and runtime risk: strict R4 parsers or generated R4 models will not have a `statusReason` property, and dropping it can lose the reason for cancellation or another status transition.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: For eligibility workflows, losing the reason for a cancelled or otherwise changed request can affect operational follow-up and auditability even though the core `status` code remains.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent why a financial request status changed, especially when cancelled.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is needed because `statusReason` is optional and preserves R4-valid instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal, representing why a request status changed, is reasonable. R6 accomplishes it with an optional, non-modifier string, so existing R4 instances that omit the element remain valid in the R6 base resource. The reported compatibility concern is reverse conversion or strict R4 consumption of new R6 content, not an R4-to-R6 breaking base-design change.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: For this calibration, a backward-compatible base R6 alternative is **not applicable**: the base R6 design already preserves R4-valid instances by making `statusReason` optional. An official R4 extension or StructureMap would be useful for preserving R6 `statusReason` when converting back to R4, but that is a cross-version mitigation and should not be counted as a less-breaking R6 base design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 extensions or conversion maps can mitigate R6-to-R4 data loss, but they are migration aids rather than base-design alternatives.

evidence.detail: No R4 local element with this id exists.

evidence.quote: Used to indicate why the status has changed.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment includes the required local fields needed to show where the new R6 `statusReason` would appear. Plain R4 has no corresponding property; an extension or local transform would be needed to preserve it.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds `CoverageEligibilityRequest.statusReason` so a request can explain why its status changed. Existing R4 instances remain valid because the field is optional, but R4 code generated from the R4 StructureDefinition will not recognize the property when consuming R6 JSON. The practical issue is reverse migration and interoperability with strict R4 systems, not forward validation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid instance that omits `statusReason` is still structurally compatible with R6. An R6-valid instance that includes `statusReason` is not representable in base R4 without extension data, and a strict R4 validator would reject the unknown element. Generated serializers may also drop the string if no extension mapping is configured.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6 migration, no value needs to be backfilled unless local policy requires status reasons for specific statuses. For R6-to-R4 migration, define an extension or conversion rule to carry the string, and test cancelled/status-changed examples so the reason is not silently discarded.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The base R6 addition is forward-compatible for R4 data, but cross-version compatibility depends on a published R4 representation. An optional extension-based bridge would have reduced data-loss risk for R4 consumers while allowing R6 to expose the field directly.

findings.title: R6 adds repeatable CoverageEligibilityRequest.event backbone with mandatory children when present

oldState.summary: R4 had no local `event` backbone on CoverageEligibilityRequest.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented requested service timing with `serviced[x]` and had no repeatable typed event/date structure.

newState.summary: R6 adds `event` 0..* with required `type` and `when[x]` children for each event repetition.

constraints.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children or both

semanticText.definition: Information code for an event with a corresponding date or period.

newState.narrativeMd: Each R6 `event` occurrence must include a `type` CodeableConcept and a `when[x]` value of `dateTime` or `Period`. The `type` binding is example strength to `ValueSet/datestype`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 event backbone is a new local child. R4 `serviced[x]` is not a true match because it is singular service timing and lacks an event type.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The parent `event` element is optional, so existing R4 instances do not become invalid in R6. However, R6 instances using typed repeatable events cannot be converted losslessly to base R4. Strict R4 parsers will reject the unknown `event` property, and mapping it to `serviced[x]` would lose the event type and possibly additional repetitions.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Eligibility events may drive timing, card, or service expectations. Dropping or flattening them can change workflow behavior even when validation still succeeds after data loss.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow multiple typed events with associated dates or periods on the eligibility request.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is needed because the new `event` backbone is optional and does not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal, supporting repeatable typed events with dates or periods, is reasonable and covers information that R4 `serviced[x]` could not represent cleanly. The R6 parent element is optional; its mandatory children apply only when new R6 `event` content is present. That creates R6-to-R4 representability risk, but not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: For the compact alternative judgment, this is **not applicable** rather than `Partial`: preserving R4-valid instances does not require an alternative because R6 leaves `event` optional. A published R4 extension or conversion map could reduce data loss for R6 event-bearing instances exchanged with R4 systems, but such tooling is migration support, not a less-breaking base R6 design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 extensions or conversion maps would improve reverse-conversion fidelity, but they are not backward-compatible base R6 design alternatives.

evidence.quote: Information code for an event with a corresponding date or period.

evidence.detail: Each event requires `type` 1..1 CodeableConcept and `when[x]` 1..1 dateTime or Period.

examples.examplesMd: The example uses text-only `CodeableConcept` for the event type because the R6 binding is example strength. R4 has no base property for the repeatable typed event; mapping only to `serviced[x]` would not preserve the type.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 introduces a repeatable `event` backbone for coded event timing. This is expressive but creates a cross-version gap because R4 has only the separate `serviced[x]` element and no event type. Implementers should not assume that all R6 event data can be collapsed into R4 service dates without semantic loss.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances remain valid in R6 because `event` is optional. R6 instances with `event` are valid only if each repetition has both `type` and `when[x]`; those instances are not valid base R4 JSON. R4 validators and generated classes will treat `event` as unknown unless extension handling or a custom model is used.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6 migration, leave `event` absent unless reliable event information exists. For R6-to-R4 migration, define a loss policy: use an extension for full fidelity, map only narrowly understood service timing into `serviced[x]`, and flag cases with multiple events or non-service event types for review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The addition is likely justified by new information requirements, but an official extension and conversion map would make the change less disruptive for R4 consumers. Without those, each implementation must choose between data loss, non-standard extensions, or rejecting R6 event-bearing requests.

findings.title: Provider comment shifts from request responsibility toward billing-provider/data-accountability semantics

oldState.summary: R4 provider was the party responsible for the eligibility request, with a comment distinguishing that party from professional responsibility for listed products/services.

semanticText.definition: The provider which is responsible for the request.
semanticText.comment: Typically this field would be 1..1 where this party is responsible for the eligibility request but not necessarily professionally responsible for the provision of the individual products and services listed below.

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 comment aligns the element with request responsibility/requestor identity and explicitly says it need not be the provider professionally responsible for the listed services.

newState.summary: R6 keeps the same cardinality and reference targets, but the comment describes accountability for data content and calls the field the Billing Provider.

semanticText.definition: The provider which is responsible for the request.
semanticText.comment: Typically this field would be 1..1 where this party is accountable for the data content within the claim but is not necessarily the facility, provider group or practitioner who provided the products and services listed within this claim resource. This field is the Billing Provider, for example, a facility, provider group, lab or practitioner.

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 definition and requirements still mention the request/requestor, but the comment introduces claim-oriented billing-provider language.

facts.oldValue: Typically this field would be 1..1 where this party is responsible for the eligibility request but not necessarily professionally responsible for the provision of the individual products and services listed below.
facts.newValue: Typically this field would be 1..1 where this party is accountable for the data content within the claim but is not necessarily the facility, provider group or practitioner who provided the products and services listed within this claim resource. This field is the Billing Provider, for example, a facility, provider group, lab or practitioner.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id, path, cardinality, type, and reference targets are unchanged; only local semantic/comment text changed materially.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Validators and generated models will not reject data because the computable shape is unchanged. The risk is semantic: systems that populate `provider` as the requestor may not be satisfying R6's billing-provider/accountability interpretation, while systems reading R6 data may treat the same reference differently in authorization or billing workflows.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Misidentifying the responsible or billing provider can affect payer routing, accountability, audit, and downstream financial decisions.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify which provider role should be supplied for financial accountability or billing context.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `provider` anchored to requestor/request responsibility and clarify billing-provider accountability with non-exclusive wording or a distinct optional concept.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying financial accountability is a reasonable R6 goal, but the R6 comment appears to redirect `provider` toward claim/billing-provider semantics while the definition and requirements still refer to request responsibility and requestor identity. Because a wording-only clarification could have preserved the R4 interpretation while explaining common billing-provider use, the semantic disruption was probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A plausible less-breaking base R6 design would retain the R4 semantics that `provider` is the party responsible for the eligibility request, then add text such as: in many billing workflows this will be the billing provider or data-accountable party. If R6 needed a separate accountability role, it could add a distinct optional element or clearly profiled concept. The separate-element path has some duplication and long-term cleanup risk, but the lower-cost wording alternative likely meets the goal without changing existing business interpretation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Clearer wording has low cost; a separate billing-provider concept adds model surface and possible overlap but avoids silently reinterpreting existing `provider` data.

evidence.detail: R4 comment describes the provider as responsible for the eligibility request and not necessarily professionally responsible for listed services.
R6 comment describes accountability for claim data content and says the field is the Billing Provider.
evidence.quote: This field is the Billing Provider

evidence.detail: R4 target profiles are Practitioner, PractitionerRole, and Organization.
R6 target profiles remain Practitioner, PractitionerRole, and Organization.

examples.examplesMd: No JSON example is needed because this is not a shape-level validation break. The same `provider` reference can be structurally valid in both versions while being interpreted as requestor responsibility in R4 and billing-provider/data-accountability in R6.

findings.narrativeMd: `CoverageEligibilityRequest.provider` keeps the same path, cardinality, type, and reference targets, but the R6 comment changes the business framing. That can surprise implementers because code and validators provide no signal that the expected role may have shifted. The wording also references a claim resource, so human review is needed to determine whether this is intentional semantic alignment across financial resources or an over-broad copied clarification.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: There is no old-valid/new-invalid validation mechanism for this finding. The same instance remains syntactically valid in both versions. The compatibility issue is behavioral: business rules, UI labels, payer routing, and auditing logic that interpret `provider` may need to change even though schemas and generated classes do not.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review how `provider` is populated and consumed. If existing R4 data uses it as the request submitter/requestor, confirm whether that party is also the R6 billing provider or accountable party. Where those roles differ, use profiles, extensions, implementation guidance, or separate local fields to avoid silently changing meaning.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because the element's computable definition did not change, a clearer backward-compatible path would have been narrative text that explicitly preserved requestor semantics while adding billing-provider guidance, or a separate element/extension for billing accountability. That would reduce semantic ambiguity without disrupting existing data interpretation.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 comment says 'claim' and 'claim resource' inside CoverageEligibilityRequest. This may be deliberate financial-resource harmonization, but it may also be a copied comment; official narrative change notes would improve confidence.

Example bindings were not fully expanded.

No local non-base invariant was found to be added, removed, or strengthened on common CoverageEligibilityRequest elements. Differences seen in `dom-*` and `ele-1` constraints are inherited base-artifact changes and excluded from findings.
The local modifier status is stable: `CoverageEligibilityRequest.status` remains a modifier, and no common local element changed modifier meaning.
Summary flags on common local elements are unchanged. The new `statusReason` element is summary=true and is covered by its addition finding.
No local slicing or slice identity changes were found in the assigned resource.
No local fixed, pattern, or default value change was found.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex-style value limit change was found.

Existing local JSON/XML element names were not renamed or removed. Serialization risk is limited to R6-added `statusReason` and `event`, which strict R4 serializers/parsers may not recognize and which are covered in findings.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Resource metadata advances from draft/trial-use FMM 2 to active/normative FMM 4
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This changes maturity and standards-status metadata, not instance shape. It does not make any R4 instance invalid by itself.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementers may treat R6 CoverageEligibilityRequest as more stable/normative and should review governance expectations, but this is not a local serialization or validation break.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Required binding URLs retarget to R6 package versions with unchanged local code sets
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The required value set references are versioned to `6.0.0-ballot4`, but the locally packaged complete code systems contain the same allowed codes as R4 for both required bindings.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Validators should load the R6 terminology package when validating R6 instances. Existing R4 `status` and `purpose` codes remain valid based on local CodeSystem comparison.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 explicitly emits mustSupport=false on local elements
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 omitted `mustSupport` on these base elements, which is equivalent to false in normal ElementDefinition processing. R6's explicit false values do not impose new conformance obligations.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators or diff tools should avoid treating explicit `false` as a newly imposed Must Support requirement.
